audit.whatIsWrong: The page claimed 'Full E-Q-W Flux cycling at melee range bypasses his Windwall entirely, turning his entire defensive kit into dead weight' — repeated in the level-3 spike and the early block. It is false, and it is the exact class of error the calibration list names (Azir soldiers vs Wind Wall).
audit.why: Ryze's Q (Overload) and E (Spell Flux) are both flagged projectile — 'can be blocked by Wind Wall-class effects'. Wind Wall blocks projectiles regardless of how close you stand; range does not defeat it. What DOES land is W (Rune Prison), which is a targeted cast on a single enemy, not a projectile. So the real rule is the inverse of what was written: root through the wall, and spend the cascade in its downtime.
audit.corrected: Every 'melee range beats Wind Wall' claim replaced with: Wind Wall eats Q and E, Rune Prison lands through it, so open W and cascade after the wall expires.

audit.whatIsWrong: The mid block called Wind Wall 'the lane's timer — once you see it deployed, that is your 8-second free window'. Steel Tempest's knock-up was described as arriving on the third stack.
audit.why: Wind Wall lasts 4 seconds and comes back every 25/23/21/19/17s — the free window is the 25-second cooldown at rank 1, not an 8-second duration. Steel Tempest knocks up at 2 stacks, not 3.
audit.corrected: 4-second duration and 25-second rank-1 cooldown written in; the knock-up moved to two stacks.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Ryze Level 1 (where the why says Yasuo trades freely with shield and Steel Tempest) and gave Yasuo Level 3 and First item (where the whys describe your loop coming online and Seraph's removing the mana gate).
audit.why: Yasuo's level 1 is free; Ryze's windows are level 3 onward and Seraph's; Yasuo reclaims it at two crit items with Last Breath. The packet chart says exactly that.
audit.corrected: Yasuo, Skill, Ryze, Skill, Ryze, Ryze, Yasuo — paired full/content rows with ratings.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Windwall' throughout the content layer, and the claim that minion bodies block his Sweeping Blade dashes.
audit.why: The ability is Wind Wall. Minions do not block Sweeping Blade — they are what he dashes THROUGH, so a thick wave helps him. The real constraint is that Sweeping Blade cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds.
audit.corrected: Name fixed; the dash want rewritten to the re-target restriction.

edits.before: At level 1 you have only Q, which is a short-range projectile he can dash under and retaliate freely — do not walk up trying to melee-range Flux stack, just last-hit and accept the first few minion waves from range. Level 2 gives you W and your first root threat; the moment he dashes toward you to complete a Steel Tempest stack, snap the root on him and fire the empowered Q into his face before he can reset another dash. By level 3 the E-Q-W Flux loop is live, and because you are fighting at melee range his Windwall does not save him — your empowered Q and W bounce AOE hit him directly, so trade every time you have E up and the wall is on cooldown.
edits.after: At level 1 you have only Q, a projectile his Wind Wall deletes outright and his dash walks under — do not walk up trying to Flux stack, just last-hit and take the first few waves from range. Level 2 gives you W and your first root threat; the moment he dashes toward you for a second Steel Tempest stack, snap the root on him — Rune Prison is targeted, so the wall cannot stop it — and fire the empowered Q before he resets another dash. By level 3 the E-Q-W loop is live, but the ordering matters: root first, then cascade, and only spend Q and E once Wind Wall's four seconds have expired.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are the mana-tax grind — your combos are online but costly pre-Seraph, and Yasuo can dash through the wave to trade whenever your W is down, so play around its cooldown and shove the wave when you can to deny his Sweeping Blade targets. At level 6 Realm Warp adds roam threat but no combat steroid, yet your combo loop is threatening enough that standing under tower lets you bait his all-in: he must dash in to trade, and a well-timed W root into cascade ends the skirmish in your favor. Treat the Windwall as the lane's timer — once you see it deployed, that is your 8-second free window to walk up and full-combo him.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are the mana-tax grind — your combos are online but costly pre-Seraph, and Yasuo dashes through the wave to trade whenever your W is down, so play around its cooldown and thin the wave to take away his Sweeping Blade stepping stones. At level 6 Realm Warp adds roam threat but no combat steroid, yet your loop is threatening enough that standing under tower baits his all-in: he must dash in to trade, and a W root into cascade ends that skirmish in your favor. Wind Wall is the lane's clock — it lasts four seconds and returns every 25 at rank 1, so the moment it expires you have twenty-plus seconds to full-combo him.

notes: This matchup carried the highest-severity error found in the slice: the page told the player his projectiles beat Wind Wall at close range. They do not — Ryze's Q and E are both flagged blockable, and only the targeted W (Rune Prison) reaches him through the wall. Anything downstream of that claim (the level-3 'trade every time' advice) was rewritten to root-first ordering. Whether Wind Wall blocks the Flux debuff's secondary spread to nearby enemies is not stated in Riot's text and is not asserted anywhere.
